item.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
item.description: This one was a banger. Not totally perfect, but a banger. I loved Agatha Christie growing up, and thought her work was awesome. I never ended up reading a Hercule Poirot novel of my own when younger so a few years ago I added a bunch of his stories to my reading list. After “The Murder on the Orient Express,” which I thought was kind of middle of the road, I took a short break. I’m happy to say I would love to read another one in the series.

item.title: CHAOS - Charles Manson, the CIA, and the Secret History of the CIA
item.description: My first non-fiction read in quite a while, and one that made me want to pick up more of them. Not only has this book been on my “To be read” list for years, I had a coworker who read it and really sold me on it. I was skeptical at first; what would this book contain that I didn’t already suspect myself or imagine could be different than every other telling of the nights that Manson family slaughtered Sharon Tate and the like. I certainly did not expect what O’Neill presents: a narrative of negligence that potentially costed the lives of seemingly innocent people. Not only their negligence of letting this family almost openly commit crimes, but of the prosecution and handling of said family.
